IRS990.ActivityOrMissionDesc: To make Cascadia a global model of sustainability.
IRS990.MissionDesc: To make the Cascadia bioregion-from Alaska to Oregon and from the Pacific to the northern Rockies-a global model of sustainability with strong communities, a green economy, and a healthy environment.
IRS990.Desc: Sightline Institute equips the people of Cascadia - including policymakers, advocates, and community leaders - with trusted, actionable research to drive long-term solutions to the region's most pressing challenges. In 2024, the Organization's work informed key policy decisions across the Northwest, including state-level clean energy reforms, new zoning measures to enable more housing options, and efforts to strengthen democratic systems and civic participation. We shared our insights widely through in-depth articles, media commentary, briefings, and public events. All research is freely available under our open-use policy. The core program areas are: climate and energy, housing and cities, democracy and elections, and farms and forests.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 11b
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Finance and Audit Committee (FAC) reviews and approves the Form 990, and forwards a copy to the Board Chair to distribute to the full Board. The Board Chair distributes it to the full Board, and informs the Executive Director (ED) that the Form 990 has been reviewed and approved by the FAC and distributed to the Board. The ED reviews the Form 990, signs it, and files it with the IRS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 12c
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Employees, board members, interns, volunteers, and contractors are required by policy to promptly disclose any conflict of interests to a supervisor or fellow board member. Board members are explicitly asked once a year if a conflict of interest exists. If a conflict of interest is determined to exist at any level, the interested parties are prohibited from making decisions regarding the relationship.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section B, line 15a
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Annually, a sub-committee of the board reviews the Executive Director's (ED) self-evaluation, meets with the ED to discuss it, and solicits feedback from and meets with senior staff to judge their perspective of the ED's effectiveness. The sub-committee then creates a report that makes a recommendation to the full Board on whether and how much to increase the ED's salary and/or authorize a bonus, based on the members' evaluation of the quality of the ED's performance.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Section C, line 19
